key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports process-window selection to reduce weld defects, thermal gradients and axial-force fluctuations in HDPE joining.
method: Develop and experimentally validate a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model of temperature, force, material flow and defects.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force responses.
Combine simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: ANN predictions achieved R² values of 0.91–0.99; 60 °C bottom preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N and raised peak temperature from 70 °C to about 100 °C.
watch_item: Reported predictive accuracy and optimal settings apply to the tested parameter space; performance beyond those conditions requires further validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
